summary: Outputs the browser viewport's width, height and aspect ratio, updating live on every window resize.
description: Screen Resolution reports the size of the browser viewport — despite the name it reads window.innerWidth/innerHeight, not the physical screen. `width` and `height` are levels in CSS pixels, `aspectRatio` is width divided by height, and all three update automatically whenever the window resizes (including device rotation). The node has no inputs.
whenToUse: Use it to drive responsive logic in the graph: feed `width` into an Expression or Condition to produce breakpoint booleans ('narrow layout?') that control visibility or layout inputs. For purely visual responsiveness, prefer the built-in sizing/variants of visual nodes; reach for this node when logic must know the viewport size.

ports.width: Number level; current viewport width in CSS pixels (window.innerWidth), updated on resize.
ports.height: Number level; current viewport height in CSS pixels (window.innerHeight), updated on resize.
ports.aspectRatio: Number level; width / height — greater than 1 in landscape, less than 1 in portrait.

patterns: `width` → Expression `width < 600` → a Group's or Text's `visible`: show compact-layout elements only on narrow viewports.
